documents.snippet: Conduct rigorous, source-grounded scholarly research with agent-based workflows and robust update safety.
paragraphs: Conduct rigorous, source-grounded scholarly research with agent-based workflows and robust update safety.
**Documentation:** https://jlcatonjr.github.io/researchteam/ · **API Reference:** https://jlcatonjr.github.io/researchteam/api-reference/

ResearchTeam is a pip-installable framework for producing well-structured research reports with verified citations, using agent-based workflows. All claims are grounded in peer-reviewed or reputable scholarly sources, with Chicago-style citations. Once installed, a derived project can receive infrastructure updates automatically — without touching user research content.
```bash pip install "researchteam @ git+https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git@v1.0.2" ```

Install the latest signed `v1.0.N` tag (currently `v1.0.2`); for a verified install from a separate tag checkout, see [`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md). `release/1.0` holds reviewed fixes queued for the next patch release: unsigned between tags, not for pinning. How branches, releases and contributions work: [`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md).
`init` scaffolds a complete project directory, seeds a neutral placeholder `brief.json`, generates a project-specific `README.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, runs `git init`, and makes an initial commit. Then:

1. Edit `brief.json` to describe your project (name, goal, `layer2_profile`, etc.). 2. Run `researchteam personalize` to regenerate `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s header from the updated `brief.json`. 3. Run `researchteam materialize` to re-render the agent team so agent bodies reflect your project's domain and identity.
```bash git clone https://github.com/jlcatonjr/researchteam.git my-research-project cd my-research-project ```
Then follow the onboarding steps in `CLAUDE.md` or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
``` researchteam init [name] [--ref REF] [--remote URL] [--vulnscan-level off|scan] ```

- `name` — directory to create (defaults to current directory if empty) - `--ref` — upstream git ref to scaffold from (default: `main`) - `--remote` — git remote URL to set as `origin` after init - `--vulnscan-level` — set `brief.json`'s `vulnerability_scanning.level` (default `scan`, from the scaffold); `remediate` is an operator choice via `agentteams --set-vulnscan`
``` researchteam update [--yes] [--dry-run] [--layer2-only | --layer1-only] [--ref REF] [--accept-upstream PATH] [--no-codex] ```

- `--yes / -y` — skip interactive confirmation; required in CI - `--dry-run` — show what would change without writing files - `--layer2-only` — only sync layer-2 files; skip `agentteams --update --merge` - `--ref` — override the upstream ref (default: the release-locked `toolchain.lock`'s verified researchteam tag, else the `.researchteam` marker, else `main`) - `--accept-upstream PATH` — take upstream's part above `## Project-Specific Notes` of an `above-notes` file the repo
ResearchTeam infrastructure is split into two independently updatable layers:
**User-owned files** (`brief.json`, `Projects/`, `references/`) are never touched by any update layer.

`README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s header are **generated per-project** from `brief.json`, not synced from upstream — `researchteam update` never re-imposes the framework's own identity on them. Regenerate them with `researchteam personalize`. `CLAUDE.md` is dual-managed: its title and *Project Purpose* header are project-owned/generated, while the fenced-preserve `researchteam:managed` block carries synced framework governance.

documents.title: Fix: the release-line candidate from a stable lock must be stable (researchteam 1.1.1)
documents.snippet: Reported by infrastructureManagement on 2026-11-09 (agentteams row 691; agentteams-6c verified it in source).
paragraphs: Reported by infrastructureManagement on 2026-11-09 (agentteams row 691; agentteams-6c verified it in source).

**Defect.** `researchteam._release.newest_on_line` keeps every tag on the line with `tag_key > current`. Because `tag_key` orders `v1.1.1-rc.1` above `v1.1.0`, a STABLE lock gets an rc as its candidate. `check_toolchain.py --release-candidate` then prints it, and the autosync gate integrates it. baseAgent #324 (v1.1.0 → v1.1.1-rc.1) shows this. It breaks the latest-stable rule: adopting an rc requires a recorded `@security` clearance.

**Fix.** - `newest_on_line(repo, current, include_prerelease=None)`: from a stable `current`, only stable tags are eligible. From an rc, newer rcs and the final stay eligible. `include_prerelease=True` is an explicit opt-in. - `check_toolchain.py --release-candidate NAME [--include-prerelease]`. The autosync gate never passes the flag. - `--write-lock --tag name=<rc>` is unchanged: a deliberate rc pin is still possible, with its own signed row.
**Tests:** stable→rc refused, stable→stable, rc→final, rc→rc, the opt-in, and the existing line tests.

**Release.** researchteam v1.1.1, a patch on release/1.1: PR to main, then the operator fast-forwards release/1.1 and signs v1.1.1. Derived repos move with `--researchteam-tag v1.1.1`, which re-syncs check_toolchain.py and installs the fixed `_release.py`. Until they do, keep autosync held for v1.1-locked repos.
